title: Structural Model for Recruitment of RIT1 to the LZTR1 E3 Ligase: Evidences from an Integrated Computational Approach.
authors: Paladino, Antonella; D'Angelo, Fulvio; Noviello, Teresa Maria Rosaria; Iavarone, Antonio; Ceccarelli, Michele
journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
one_liner_zh: 该文用分子建模、对接和MD研究LZTR1与RIT1蛋白-蛋白互作，虽涉及泛素连接酶体系而非TF-DNA，且无AI/物理模拟方法创新，仅部分可借鉴界面建模思路。
abstract: Leucine-zipper transcription regulator 1 (LZTR1) is a highly mutated tumor suppressor gene, involved in the pathogenesis of several cancer types and developmental disorders. In proteasomal degradation, it acts as an adaptor protein responsible for the recognition and recruitment of substrates to be ubiquitinated in Cullin3-RING ligase E3 (CRL3) machinery. LZTR1 belongs to the BTB-Kelch family, a multi-domain protein where the Kelch propeller plays as the substrate recognition region and for which no experimental structure has been solved. Recently, large effort mutational analyses pointed to the role of disease-associated LZTR1 mutations in the RAS/MAPK signaling pathway and RIT1, a small Ras-related GTPase protein, has been identified by mass spectroscopy to interact with LZTR1. Hence, a better understanding of native structure, molecular mechanism, and substrate specificity would help clarifying the role of LZTR1 in pathological diseases, thus promoting advancement in the development of novel therapeutic strategies. Here, we address the interaction model between adaptor LZTR1 and substrate RIT1 by applying an integrated computational approach, including molecular modeling and docking techniques. We observe that the interaction model LZTR1-RIT1 is stabilized by an electrostatic bond network established between the two protein surfaces, which is reminiscent of homologous ubiquitin ligases complexes. Then, running MD simulations, we characterize differential conformational dynamics of the multi-domain LZTR1, offering interesting implications on the mechanistic role of specific point mutations. We identify G248R and R283Q as damaging mutations involved in the recognition process of the substrate RIT1 and R412C as a possible allosteric mutation from the Kelch to the C-term BTB-domain. Our findings provide important structural insights on targeting CRL3s for drug discovery.
abstract_zh: 亮氨酸拉链转录调控因子1（LZTR1）是一个高频突变的肿瘤抑制基因，参与多种癌症类型和发育障碍的发病机制。在蛋白酶体降解过程中，它作为衔接蛋白，负责识别并招募底物，以供Cullin3-RING连接酶E3（CRL3）机制进行泛素化。LZTR1属于BTB-Kelch家族，是一种多结构域蛋白，其中Kelch螺旋桨结构作为底物识别区域，且该区域尚无实验解析的结构。近期，大规模的突变分析研究指出，疾病相关的LZTR1突变在RAS/MAPK信号通路中发挥作用，并通过质谱分析鉴定出RIT1（一种小型Ras相关GTPase蛋白）与LZTR1相互作用。因此，更深入地了解其天然结构、分子机制和底物特异性，将有助于阐明LZTR1在病理疾病中的作用，从而推动新型治疗策略的开发。在此，我们通过应用整合计算策略（包括分子建模和对接技术），探讨了衔接蛋白LZTR1与底物RIT1之间的相互作用模型。我们观察到，LZTR1-RIT1相互作用模型通过两个蛋白表面之间建立的静电键网络得以稳定，这类似于同源泛素连接酶复合物。随后，通过运行分子动力学（MD）模拟，我们表征了多结构域LZTR1的差异构象动态，为特定点突变的机制作用提供了有趣启示。我们鉴定出G248R和R283Q为参与底物RIT1识别过程的有害突变，而R412C可能是从Kelch结构域到C端BTB结构域的变构突变。我们的发现为靶向CRL3进行药物发现提供了重要的结构见解。
